product.name: Relay
product.domain: watching deployments go out and catching the ones that go wrong
product.audience: an on-call platform engineer, usually with the dashboard on a second monitor while doing something else

brand.rationale: A cyan-leaning blue at OKLCH hue 195, chosen because the status roles already own green, amber and red on this product — a deployment dashboard is mostly status, so the accent has to stay clear of all three signal hues to avoid reading as a fourth status. The neutral is cool (hue 250) rather than warm: this surface is watched on a dark second monitor for hours, and a cool ramp sits back further behind the status colours.

decisions.what: Dark is the primary designed mode; light is designed second, not derived by inversion.
decisions.why: The screen lives on a second monitor during on-call rotations that run overnight. Light mode still gets a hand-tuned ramp because incident reviews happen in daylight and get screenshotted into documents.

decisions.what: The accent is cyan (hue 195), deliberately not green, amber or red.
decisions.why: On a product where most of the pixels are status, an accent near a signal hue gets read as a signal. Cyan is far enough from success green (150) to never be mistaken for it at a glance.

decisions.what: The neutral ramp is cool (hue 250), unlike the warm default.
decisions.why: A warm neutral competes with amber. On a status-dense dark surface the ramp has to recede completely, and a cool grey does that better next to warning colours.
